title: Intrinsic Self-correction for Enhanced Morality: An Analysis of Internal Mechanisms and the Superficial Hypothesis
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured the reduction of stereotypical bias in religious contexts using a fairness score. The experiments analyzed how moral self-correction instructions improve the model's ability to provide unbiased answers in multiple-choice questions related to religion.
findings: The study found that intrinsic moral self-correction significantly improves the fairness score of Mistral-7B on the religion dimension of the BBQ benchmark, increasing performance from a baseline of approximately 0.825 to 0.900 in the first round of correction. The analysis of internal hidden states showed they are a strong predictor (98% accuracy) for estimating the effectiveness of different self-correction instructions for reducing religious bias.
references: Guillaume Alain and Yoshua Bengio. 2016. Understanding intermediate layers using linear classifier probes. arXiv preprint arXiv:1610.01644.
